subject: EU onboarding + APAC standby: scope, timelines, and term amendment
messages:
From: Elena Martinez <elena@healthcore.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: HealthCore renewal / EU + APAC requirements

Hi Irene,

We're starting our renewal conversations for the HC platform contract and we have two priority asks from the product and compliance teams: first, we want the EU region to be the primary residency for EU traffic (data-at-rest in EU and processing in-region) starting Q1 next year; second, we need APAC as a warm-standby/failover region for traffic spikes and DR.

High level asks: 
- Confirm whether Redwood can add an EU primary residency contract amendment and provide SOC2 + data flow mapping for the EU nodes.
- Pricing for APAC warm-standby (committed v. standby capacity) and how billing would apply for occasional failover traffic.
- Any changes to standard SLA/penalties when traffic crosses region boundaries during failover.

Our procurement lead (procurement@healthcore.com) and Marc Dupont (EMEA infra lead) are on standby; I'll need an initial SOW and cost estimate by the first week of November to stay on our renewal cadence.

I've attached a short list of internal compliance questions and the draft SOW template we use.

Thanks,
Elena Martinez
Director of Platform Strategy
HealthCore

Attachments: HC_sow_template.docx (template), compliance_questions.pdf

From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
To: Elena Martinez <elena@healthcore.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-22T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: HealthCore renewal / EU + APAC requirements

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear asks and timeline. High-level plan and open items below.

Proposal (two-phase):
1) Phase A (EU residency):
   - Spin up EU-dedicated tenancy for HealthCore (customer-isolated vpc, EU-only storage)
   - Data residency controls: KMS in EU, audit logs forwarded to customer-controlled S3, SOC2 evidence packet (we can provide)
   - Estimated go-live: mid-Jan 2027 (depends on contract sign + infra lead coordination)

2) Phase B (APAC warm-standby):
   - Standby pool with reserved burst capacity for failover; billing model options: reserved-burst (monthly commit + usage overage) or pure standby (lower commit, higher failover usage rate)
   - Failover routing policy and cross-region SLOs: recommend a documented runbook plus a 99.5% regional availability SLA with failover exceptions called out in an exhibit.

Open items we need from HealthCore:
- Expected steady RPS and peak token rate per region (helps size standby).
- Procurement contact for contract amendment and PO cadence.
- Any regulatory constraints beyond EU residency (e.g., subject access, retention windows).

I attached an initial SOW skeleton and a capacity workbook request template for sizing. Ben and Jordan — if you can review the capacity assumptions and pricing bands, please flag anything we should change for HealthCore's scale.

I'll aim to return an updated SOW & two pricing options by Friday Nov 5th.

Best,
Irene Choi
Head of Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference

Attachments: HC-SOW-v2.pdf

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-25T08:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: HealthCore renewal / EU + APAC requirements

Irene — quick technical sizing notes (attaching workbook):

- HealthCore reported steady 30 req/s (text-gen) with 2.5k avg tokens and 3x peaks during spikes. For EU primary we recommend: 2x insured model instances (m-sku) + autoscale headroom for prefix-cache priming.
- APAC standby: recommend a 40% reserved capacity of EU baseline for warm standby. This lets us handle a regional failover for routing bursts without immediate scale-up latency.
- Billing suggestion: Offer two SKUs — Reserved Standby (monthly commit 40% baseline, carry-forward credits for unused reserved capacity) or On-Demand Failover (no commit, higher per-minute burst rate).

Attached: capacity_workbook.xlsx (sizing, cost simulation).

On the SLA language — Jordan, can you draft a short exhibit clarifying that failover traffic routed to APAC will be treated under the same availability window, but that data residency guarantees apply only to primary region unless explicit mirror/replication is purchased.

Ben
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments: capacity_workbook.xlsx

From: Elena Martinez <elena@healthcore.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Cc: Marc Dupont <m.dupont@healthcore-eu.com>, HealthCore Procurement <procurement@healthcore.com>
Date: 2026-11-02T10:55:00+01:00
Subject: Re: HealthCore renewal / EU + APAC requirements

Thanks — this all looks reasonable. Procurement is looping in our contracts lead (procurement@healthcore.com) and Marc will coordinate infra timelines. A couple of clarifications: 

- SOC2 / evidence: procurement asked for the most recent SOC2 report and a short data flow diagram showing where keys and logs reside.
- Retention: default retention is fine for now but we may require a 90-day logs retention SLA for auditability in the EU tenancy.
- Timeline constraint: EU go-live needs to be before March 1, 2027. Can you confirm that mid-Jan is still realistic with procurement and sign by Nov 15?

Procurement says they can accept a two-exhibit approach (main contract + regional exhibit) but need the amendment language to be clear about cross-region billing. Please send the commercial exhibits and a DocuSign-ready signature package.

Onward,
Elena

Hi Elena / Sam / Marc —

Attached are the items we agreed on after internal review:
- HC-SOW-v2.pdf (SOW with phase A/B split, EU residency config, APAC standby options)
- Capacity workbook (sizing and pricing bands)
- SOC2_report_redwood.pdf (current report)

Key commercial notes:
- Term amendment: 12-month renewal with an EU regional exhibit added. APAC standby can be purchased as a Reserved Standby SKU (40% baseline commit) or as On-Demand Failover. Pricing exhibits included in SOW (see sections 3.2/3.3).
- Data residency: EU tenancy will ensure at-rest storage in EU and KMS keys scoped to EU. Cross-region failover will route user traffic to APAC only under DDoS/latency failover or scheduled drills; replication of data to APAC requires an explicit replication addendum and will carry separate consent and cost.
- SLA language: Exhibit B clarifies failover handling. Availability credit calculus remains unchanged, but incident classification differs if failover routing is invoked per runbook.

Next steps:
1) Sam / procurement — please review the attached PO term sheet and sign via DocuSign here: https://docusign.net/REDWOOD/HC-9231-sign
2) Marc / infra — we propose a planning call the week of Nov 22 to lock cutover windows and runbook ownership. 
3) Redwood ops will provide a runbook (DR drill checklist + routing playbook) before the planning call.

If you want, I can drop the SOW into your Drive folder and we'll iterate on redlines there.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this on contract.

Best,
Irene Choi
Head of Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
